title: Unexpected Results
description: Rules for evaluating results that appear to be unrelated to or unexpectedly different from what the user queried. An unexpected result is one where the connection between query and result is not obvious.

decision_logic.condition: There is a clear, logical connection between the query and the result (e.g., common abbreviation, DBA name, known alias)
decision_logic.notes: Connection exists — result is not truly unexpected once the relationship is understood

decision_logic.condition: There is a weak or indirect connection (e.g., result is at the same address, has a related name, serves similar purpose)
decision_logic.notes: Some connection exists but it is not obvious

decision_logic.condition: Result is at the correct location but is a different entity entirely (e.g., building at the address, not the business)
decision_logic.notes: Location match only, not a name/entity match

decision_logic.condition: Result has no meaningful connection to the query
decision_logic.notes: Truly unexpected and irrelevant — no connection can be found

exceptions: Results that show the parent company of a queried subsidiary may be Excellent if parent is well-known
Rebranded businesses may still rate Excellent if the old name is in the result's description
Seasonal or event-based results that match query intent may rate higher

calibration_examples.reasoning: The business was rebranded but previous name is noted — clear connection, step 1
Weak connection — houses some city functions but is not city hall, step 2

conditions: No connection to a pizza restaurant
calibration_examples.reasoning: No meaningful connection between a pizza restaurant and a park — step 4
